The missing files don't exist anywhere. They're simply absent from the repository. This is a genuine source defect. But wait - maybe the `.gitlab` directory has something, or maybe there's a sync script. Let me reconsider whether build is even required by the guide's primary method.

The primary guide method uses `composer dev`, which runs `npm run dev` (Vite dev server). The Vite dev server would also fail when it tries to compile NavUser.vue. But maybe the app loads fine because MainPage doesn't import AppSidebar, and Vite only transforms modules on demand. In dev server mode, Vite lazily transforms. The browser loads MainPage.vue which imports Navigation, Sensor, Ochsi, HomeInfoCard, SensorCard — none of which use the layout. So the dev server would only error if something imports NavUser.

But wait, is the layout used? MainPage.vue doesn't use a layout at all. Let me verify what MainPage renders. It doesn't import AppLayout. So the missing components are only referenced by unused files (AppHeader, AppSidebar, AppLayout, Dashboard).

So for the actual application route `/`, `npm run dev` (Vite dev server) might work. But `npm run build` builds ALL modules reachable from inputs? Vite build with `laravel-vite-plugin` input `resources/js/app.ts` uses `import.meta.glob('./pages/**/*.vue')` — glob includes ALL pages (Dashboard.vue), which imports AppLayout → AppSidebar → NavUser → UserMenuContent and AppHeader → UserMenuContent. So build fails.

Hmm, but the app's actual page MainPage works in dev.

Given the task is "install the software," I should get it running. The build failure means production build isn't possible and even `composer dev` might work but Vite dev may fail on demand. Let me test the dev server / php artisan serve + vite.

Actually, more important: is this missing file a real bug in upstream? Let me double-check by looking at whether maybe those files should be `.ts` or in a different path. The imports are `@/components/UserMenuContent.vue` and `./UserMenuContent.vue`, and `@/components/UserInfo.vue`. They're just missing.

Let me check the internal sync: maybe the public repo intentionally omits them. But that breaks build.

Let me try the actual primary method `composer dev` to see if the app runs. But composer dev runs queue:listen, pail, and vite concurrently. In a headless environment that's fine, but it blocks. I'll instead run `php artisan serve` and `npm run dev` in background, then curl the page.

Actually wait — maybe the missing components issue can be avoided: Vite dev only compiles on demand. The homepage `/` renders MainPage without a layout. Let me test.

Let me start php artisan serve and npm run dev, then curl.

Actually, before that, let me reconsider: could the missing files be intentionally part of the benchmark environment (i.e., the repo at this commit genuinely is broken and the expected outcome is failure)? Or maybe I should create them? The task says install; the guide doesn't mention creating files. But a missing source file that breaks the build is a repo defect.

Let me check upstream GitLab more carefully — maybe the repo has these files but under different capitalization, or the sync branch has them. Let me list all files in the sync branch remotely.

Let me fetch the merge request 8 branch.

Actually I already fetched sync/v1.0.1 into FETCH_HEAD. Let me list its tree.

git ls-tree -r FETCH_HEAD --name-only | grep "resources/js/components" | grep -i -E "user|menu"

echo "=== does sync tree have AppSidebar? ==="
git ls-tree -r FETCH_HEAD --name-only | grep -E "AppSidebar.vue|NavUser.vue|UserInfo"

git ls-tree -r HEAD --name-only | grep "resources/js/components/" | grep -v "ui/" > /tmp/head_c.txt
git ls-tree -r FETCH_HEAD --name-only | grep "resources/js/components/" | grep -v "ui/" > /tmp/sync_c.txt
diff /tmp/head_c.txt /tmp/sync_c.txt
